# JAQA

> Public-source triage for global risk, finance, insurance/reinsurance counterparties, procurement, bids, awards, regulations, events, and supply-chain exposure.

JAQA is a privacy-first web workspace for investigating public evidence about organizations, countries, ports, vulnerabilities, tenders, regulations and global risk events. It queries 19 verified public data sources directly from your browser, includes a photorealistic 3D globe (JAQA Eye View) and a Global Monitor of 18 official public feeds, and links out to official sources for everything else. It does not store searches, and it does not give credit, sanctions, insurance, legal or investment determinations.

## Features

- **Situation Room**: A command-center view with an interactive evidence globe, a live wire of public feeds (earthquakes, exploited vulnerabilities, US regulatory notices, ECB reference rates) and the signals from your current investigation.
- **3D Globe (JAQA Eye View)**: JAQA Eye View at /globe/: a photorealistic 3D globe with live aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, wildfires, weather, space launches, public cameras and sensor styles (CRT, NVG, FLIR).
- **3D evidence globe**: Inside the workspace, your session’s evidence — seismic events, places, the current subject and monitor events — on a 3D Earth with bundled Natural Earth imagery, so the view makes no third-party requests.
- **Global Monitor**: Latest headlines from official publishers (UN, WHO, GDACS, NASA EONET, USGS, NOAA NHC, CISA, UK NCSC, ECB, Federal Reserve, SEC, Bank of England, BIS, WTO, US and UK travel advice), an event map, the countries named in the headlines and an ECB FX board.
- **Organization & counterparty evidence**: Across the workspace: legal-entity (GLEIF LEI) records and parents, SEC filings and 8-K event signals, court dockets, US federal awards, environmental enforcement and product-recall records — each with its source, retrieval time and match confidence.
- **Risk universes**: A Global Risk Universe of 82 domains and a Finance Risk Universe of 32 domains, each mapped to the public sources that can evidence it and to the gaps where none can.
- **Insurance & procurement lenses**: Insurer, reinsurer, broker, captive and ILS context, plus tenders, awards, grants, PPPs and concessions — with official link-outs where no verified API exists.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is JAQA?

JAQA is a privacy-first web workspace for investigating public evidence about organizations, countries, ports, vulnerabilities, tenders, regulations and global risk events. It queries 19 verified public data sources directly from your browser, includes a photorealistic 3D globe (JAQA Eye View) and a Global Monitor of 18 official public feeds, and links out to official sources for everything else. It does not store searches, and it does not give credit, sanctions, insurance, legal or investment determinations.

### Where does JAQA’s data come from?

From public sources only. 19 public APIs are called live from your browser after their browser access (CORS) and response shape were verified from the jaqa.life origin. 18 official feeds are fetched by the JAQA server for the Global Monitor after a separate verification run. Everything else — including paid, login-only and unverified sources — is an official link-out. The full list is on the Sources page.

### Does JAQA store or track my searches?

No. JAQA has no accounts, cookies, browser storage, service workers or analytics. Workspace searches go straight from your browser to public data providers and are never sent to or logged by JAQA, or written into the URL. Clear Session wipes the in-memory state.

### What is the 3D globe?

It is JAQA Eye View, at jaqa.life/globe/. It shows a photorealistic 3D Earth with live aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, wildfires, weather, space launches and public cameras, with CRT, NVG and FLIR sensor styles. JAQA can open it at the location you are investigating. The workspace also has its own 3D evidence globe, which plots your session’s evidence on bundled imagery, without third-party requests.

### What is the Global Monitor?

A live dashboard of 18 verified official feeds — for example the UN, WHO, GDACS, NASA EONET, USGS, CISA, the ECB, the Federal Reserve, the SEC and US and UK travel advice. It shows headlines with links to the publisher, an event map from publisher-supplied coordinates, the countries named in the headlines and an ECB FX board. Headlines are shown as published; JAQA does not rank, summarize or verify them.

### Does JAQA give credit scores, sanctions clearance or advice?

No. JAQA shows public evidence with its source, date and match confidence. It does not produce credit scores, sanctions or AML clearance, insurance, underwriting or claims decisions, bid or award predictions, or legal, investment or treasury advice. A missing public record never means “clear”.

### Which regions does JAQA cover?

Global sources such as GLEIF, the World Bank, USGS, Open-Meteo, GDELT, Wikidata and the Global Monitor feeds cover most countries. Several deep sources are US-specific (SEC filings, USAspending awards, the Federal Register, CPSC and NHTSA recalls, CourtListener, EPA ECHO). For other jurisdictions JAQA links to the official registries and portals.

### How does JAQA verify a data source?

A source is used live only after automated checks pass: real requests from the production origin must return the expected data with browser-access (CORS) headers. Monitor feeds are fetched and parsed with the production parser. Results are committed to the code, and sources that fail stay link-out only. Each source shows its status in the Coverage Console.

### Does JAQA work on phones?

Yes. The workspace, the Global Monitor and these pages adapt to phone screens. The 3D globe needs a browser with WebGL; it runs on current phones, but it is heavier than the rest of the site.

### Is JAQA affiliated with the data providers?

No. JAQA is an independent interface to public data. Naming a publisher as a source does not imply any affiliation or endorsement. Open-source components and their licences are listed on the Licences page.

## Privacy

- No accounts, cookies, local storage, browser databases, service workers, analytics or tracking pixels.
- Workspace searches go directly from your browser to the selected public data providers. They are never sent to JAQA, never written into the URL and never stored.
- The JAQA server only fetches fixed, allowlisted official feeds (Global Monitor) and serves the 3D globe’s data providers. It writes no access logs.
- Clear Session wipes everything in memory. Closing the tab does the same.
- Hosting providers and data providers may keep their own infrastructure logs under their own policies.

## Live public APIs (19)

- GLEIF LEI API — https://www.gleif.org/
- World Bank Indicators API — https://data.worldbank.org/
- USGS Earthquake Catalog (FDSN) — https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/map/
- Open-Meteo (forecast + geocoding) — https://open-meteo.com/
- NOAA / National Weather Service API — https://www.weather.gov/
- CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities — https://www.cisa.gov/
- CPSC Recalls API — https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls
- NHTSA Recalls API — https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls
- USAspending API — https://www.usaspending.gov/
- Federal Register API — https://www.federalregister.gov/
- SEC EDGAR submissions — https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/
- EPA ECHO facility search — https://echo.epa.gov/
- CourtListener (Free Law Project) — https://www.courtlistener.com/
- OpenStreetMap Overpass API — https://www.openstreetmap.org/
- Wikidata — https://www.wikidata.org/
- Wikipedia REST API — https://en.wikipedia.org/
- NIST National Vulnerability Database — https://nvd.nist.gov/
- ECB Data Portal API — https://data.ecb.europa.eu/
- GDELT DOC 2.0 API — https://www.gdeltproject.org/

## Global Monitor feeds (18)

- UN News — all stories — United Nations — https://news.un.org/
- UN News — peace and security — United Nations — https://news.un.org/
- WTO news — World Trade Organization — https://www.wto.org/
- GDACS disaster alerts — GDACS (UN / European Commission) — https://www.gdacs.org/
- NASA EONET open natural events — NASA Earth Observatory — https://eonet.gsfc.nasa.gov/
- USGS significant earthquakes — 30 days — U.S. Geological Survey — https://earthquake.usgs.gov/
- NHC Atlantic tropical cyclones — NOAA National Hurricane Center — https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/
- NHC Eastern Pacific tropical cyclones — NOAA National Hurricane Center — https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/
- WHO news releases — World Health Organization — https://www.who.int/
- CISA cybersecurity advisories — U.S. CISA — https://www.cisa.gov/
- UK NCSC news and advisories — UK National Cyber Security Centre — https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/
- ECB press releases — European Central Bank — https://www.ecb.europa.eu/
- Federal Reserve press releases — U.S. Federal Reserve Board — https://www.federalreserve.gov/
- SEC press releases — U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission — https://www.sec.gov/
- Bank of England news — Bank of England — https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/
- BIS press releases — Bank for International Settlements — https://www.bis.org/
- U.S. travel advisories — U.S. Department of State — https://travel.state.gov/
- UK foreign travel advice — UK FCDO (GOV.UK) — https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice
